cues.summary: Dallas, October 19, 1985. The first store opens.
cues.text: The first Blockbuster opened in Dallas on October 19, 1985.[^20]

still.alt: A disc of small lights labeled 1988, about 400 stores, 1 light = 1 store.

cues.summary: Some 400 stores by 1988. Late fees were $692.6M in 1999.
cues.text: By 1988 it had some 400 stores.[^20] In 1999 late fees were $692.6M, 15.5% of revenue.[^2]

still.alt: A cartoon executive hiding a laugh behind his fist. On-screen text: He was struggling not to laugh, as Marc Randolph tells it.

cues.summary: 2000: Netflix asks $50M to be bought, in Marc Randolph’s account.
cues.text: By Marc Randolph’s account, Netflix offered itself to Blockbuster for $50M in September 2000.[^18]

cues.summary: In Randolph’s account, Blockbuster turns the offer down.
cues.text: It was turned down. Randolph writes that John Antioco “was struggling not to laugh.”[^18]

cues.summary: The meeting is Marc Randolph’s account.
cues.text: The meeting is Marc Randolph’s account.

still.alt: A disc of lights labeled 2004, 9,094 stores in 25 countries, $905.6M paid out to shareholders with borrowed money, long-term debt $1,119.7M at the end of 2004.

cues.text: Blockbuster ended 2004 with 9,094 stores in 25 countries, the most it ever had.[^6]

still.alt: A receipt listing the 2004 borrowing, $905.6M paid to shareholders, and long-term debt of $75.1M in 2003 and $1,119.7M in 2004.

cues.summary: 2004: about $905.6M to shareholders, funded by borrowing.
cues.text: That year it paid shareholders about $905.6M, funded by new borrowing.[^5]

cues.summary: Long-term debt rises from $75.1M to $1,119.7M in a year.
cues.text: Long-term debt rose from $75.1M to $1,119.7M in a year.[^6]

cues.summary: Net losses in every year from 1997 to 2010 except 2006.
cues.text: It reported a net loss in every year from 1997 to 2010 except 2006.[^2][^6][^9][^10]

still.alt: The sign with most of its letters dark. On-screen text: 2010: Chapter 11, nearly $1 billion in debt.

cues.summary: September 23, 2010: Chapter 11, nearly $1 billion in debt.
cues.text: On September 23, 2010 it filed for Chapter 11 with nearly $1 billion of debt.[^11]

still.alt: The disc of lights almost dark, labeled 2014, about 50 franchised stores.

cues.summary: The corporate stores close by January 2014.
cues.text: Dish closed the corporate stores by January 2014.[^27]

cues.summary: About 50 franchises remain, then close one by one.
cues.text: About 50 franchised stores stayed open.[^27][^28] They closed one by one.[^29][^30]
